text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The foreign secretaries of Pakistan and India will meet in New Delhi from March 28 to 31, foreign office said in Islamabad.
- Formal meetings between the visiting International Monetary Fund (IMF) review team and the government officials will commence in Islamabad on Friday.
- The Privatisation Commission has said the government is determined to move on quickly towards the privatisation of major units.
- The Karachi Cotton Association has urged the government to immediately allow hedge trading in cotton.
- The Imperial Chemical Industries is planning to invest further in Pakistan, says ICI executive director R.J. Margetts.

- The ruling Pakistan Muslim League party has given an assurance to Mohajir National Movement that the Biharis stranded in Bangladesh would be repatriated and Mohajir quota in government jobs would be raised to 11.5 percent.
- Philippines President Fidel Ramos will reach Islamabad Friday for a three-day visit.
- Pakistan is expecting an enhanced assistance of up to $2.8 billion from Aid-to-Pakistan Consortium which meets in Paris from April 22 to 23.
- Pakistan has collected $90 million on the appeal of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif for national debt retirement programme.
- Cash-strapped government may defer a few of the private power projects having a cumulative generation capacity of 3,000 megawatts.
- Austrian firms are eager to lend a helping hand to Pakistan in the exploration of oil and gas, trade commissioner of Austria in Pakistan F. Schmirmaul told Karachi Chamber of Commerce and Industry.
- The federal cabinet has approved a package of draft legislation and administrative measures to combat lawlessness and strengthen the accountability process.
